title: Bias in Large Language Models: Origin, Evaluation, and Mitigation

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewing evaluation methods such as coreference resolution accuracy on gendered pronouns, counterfactual testing using name substitution, sentiment analysis toward gendered contexts, and fairness metrics like Equal Opportunity.

Reviewing methods that assess age-based assumptions in coreference resolution, analyze sentiment classification of texts associated with older individuals, and evaluate job application acceptance/rejection rates based on age stereotypes.

Reviewing assessments of model performance on cultural idioms, misclassification rates of regional dialects and language variants (such as AAVE), and geographic disparities in recommender systems and machine translation.

Reviewing techniques like counterfactual testing by manipulating first names in high-stakes decision-making (e.g., hiring), measuring disparate word error rates in speech recognition, and evaluating allocational harms in healthcare recommendations.
Reviewing evaluations that probe conversational LLMs with politically charged questions to measure political preferences and testing regional bias in political text classification.
Reviewing assessments of toxicity generation from religion-based prompts (e.g., Muslim-violence bias) and evaluating counterfactual data augmentation by swapping religious terms.
